items.title: Library supplement: Gaussian features, means and actual gradients

source.anchor: Complete source-only.json: A1-A4, D1-D6, C1-C7 and T1-T6.
source.attribution: Original exposition extracting a shared representation from existing Gaussian potential calculus; no primary-textbook theorem or novelty claim.

items.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel structure, let \(\gamma=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\), and let \(S=\{w\in E:\|w\|=1\}\). Let \(P\) be a probability measure on \(E\times\mathbb R\) whose first marginal is \(\gamma\). Fix a real polynomial \(p\), and assume the actual response \((x,y)\mapsto y\) belongs to \(H=L^2(P;\mathbb R)\). Define the literal feature and directional derivative by \(f_w(x,y)=p(\langle w,x\rangle)\) and \(df_{w,v}(x,y)=p^{\prime}(\langle w,x\rangle)\langle v,x\rangle\). All these functions belong to \(H\). There exist one family of continuous linear maps \(D(w):E\to H\) and positive constants \(M_1,M_2\), chosen before every parameter law and every subsequent evaluation point, with the following properties. Writing \(F(w)=[f_w]\), we have \(D(w)v=[df_{w,v}]\) and \(F\) has Fréchet derivative \(D(w)\) at every ambient \(w\). The displayed operator bounds hold on the closed unit ball. For every probability \(\rho\) on \(S\), all scalar sections defining the predictor are integrable, \(F|_S\) is Bochner integrable, and the predictor composed with the first-coordinate map belongs to \(H\), with class equal to its Bochner mean \(m_\rho\). The literal scalar potential has an integrable defining integrand at every ambient \(w\); it equals \(2\langle m_\rho-\ell,F(w)\rangle_H\) and has actual ambient gradient \(2D(w)^*(m_\rho-\ell)\) there. On the unit sphere, subtracting the normal component gives the final displayed projection formula. The same \(D,M_1,M_2\) is used throughout.
assumptions: \(E\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed space with its Borel measurable structure. Completeness follows from finite dimension. No positive-dimension or nonempty-sphere hypothesis is imposed.

\(E\times\mathbb R\) has its product measurable structure; \(P\) is a probability measure and \(P\circ\mathrm{fst}^{-1}=\operatorname{stdGaussian}(E)\), the centered Gaussian with identity covariance.
\(p\in\mathbb R[X]\) is any finite polynomial. No coefficient normalization, degree bound or parity condition is assumed.
The actual response \((x,y)\mapsto y\) is square-integrable under \(P\). Independence of response and input is not required.

\(S\) has its subtype Borel structure. Every parameter law \(\rho\) is a probability on \(S\). Ambient derivative and potential statements range over all \(w,v\in E\); the operator bounds are restricted to the closed unit ball and the projection identity to \(w\in S\).

The feature and directional-derivative membership witnesses, \(D\), and \(M_1,M_2>0\) are conclusions, selected after \(E,P,p\) and the input hypotheses but before every \(\rho,w,u,v\). No law-dependent re-choice is made. No prescribed numerical or dimension-free bounds are claimed.

obligations.label: Actual joint Gaussian L2 feature representation and literal potential gradient

bindings.boundary: This interface supplies actual L² classes, their Bochner mean, an ambient gradient and its explicit unit-sphere projection. An installed manifold-gradient identification is separate. No transport estimate, numerical operator constant, empirical rate, stochastic process or convergence theorem is added. The polynomial and actual response L² assumptions remain explicit. The result is a shared mathematical supplement and carries no primary-textbook chapter completion claim.

assumption_deltas.reason: Qualitative bounds hold only on the closed unit ball, while differentiability and the actual potential/gradient identity hold throughout the ambient space.

assumption_deltas.source: Actual L2 classes and Bochner mean; literal potential and unit-sphere projection.
assumption_deltas.lean: MemLp.toLp quotient classes, mean defined by the Bochner integral, actual Mathlib gradient with HasGradientAt and explicit normal subtraction.
assumption_deltas.reason: Class equality is almost-everywhere representative equality. The potential identity is pointwise in the weight. No intrinsic manifold identification or transport estimate is added.
